insights.topic: Verified purchase signals vs. probabilistic targeting
insights.insight: The protocol has generated 12,411 cryptographically verified purchase receipts across physical retail, dining, fuel, warehouse, and SaaS — each one a confirmed transaction, not an inferred intent. At a $5+ CPM market rate for probabilistic signals, that volume of deterministic data represents a structurally different asset class for audience targeting.

Cumulative verified GMV stands at $996,004 with $3,996 remaining — less than a single average inflow cycle at current throughput rates. The milestone is arithmetic, not speculative, and signals the protocol has crossed from proof-of-concept into measurable commerce infrastructure.

The 7-day GMV trough of $105,195 on April 17 was caused by high-volume April 10 receipts rolling out of the window simultaneously — a mechanical distortion, not an underlying demand drop. The metric has since recovered to $117,684, suggesting underlying throughput is stabilizing.

insights.topic: Velocity deceleration with early reversal signal
insights.insight: Token velocity fell from a peak of 1.241x on April 12 to a trough of 0.819x on April 17 — the sharpest single-cycle deceleration on record — but the most recent reading shows a modest recovery to 0.855x with acceleration climbing to 1.013x. One data point is not confirmation; the next heartbeat is the test.

The network has now produced three consecutive 7-CBSA expansion pulses, a pattern that suggests coordinated or incentivized user acquisition rather than organic drift. For brand marketers, this pulse-then-consolidate behavior indicates plannable geographic rollout rather than unpredictable scatter.

insights.topic: SaaS subscriptions as a new receipt category
insights.insight: Digital SaaS subscriptions entered the protocol's verified receipt set on April 9 — the first non-physical-commerce category in the network's history. This expands the targeting surface beyond brick-and-mortar into software spend, a signal set that is nearly absent from traditional retail data partnerships.
